name: Relfydess
lead: Relfydess (relabotulinumtoxinA) is a ready-to-use liquid botulinum toxin type A made by Galderma, developed with a technology the company calls PEARL to produce a complex-free formulation.[1] Unlike freeze-dried toxins, it does not require reconstitution.[1]

Its Phase 3 READY-1 trial enrolled adults with moderate-to-severe glabellar lines, randomized 3 to 1 to relabotulinumtoxinA or placebo over six months, and reported patient-assessed effectiveness and satisfaction.[1] A published 2026 case report describes off-label use for Frey's syndrome.[2]

paras: The product is presented as a liquid toxin that is ready to inject, made through PEARL technology, which the authors of the READY-1 report describe as yielding a highly effective, complex-free formulation.[1]

In READY-1, adults with moderate-to-severe glabellar lines were randomized 3:1 to relabotulinumtoxinA or placebo in a six-month study. A 2025 paper in Aesthetic Surgery Journal reported the patient-assessed outcomes for line improvement and satisfaction.[1] A 2026 case report described a 72-year-old man treated off-label with intradermal injections for gustatory sweating after parotidectomy.[2]
Adverse-event findings from the trials were not reviewed for this entry. Botulinum toxins as a class are prescription-only.[1]

Treatment of Frey's Syndrome With "Ready to Use Liquid" Relabotulinumtoxin A (Relfydess)

card.summary: Galderma's ready-to-use liquid botulinum toxin for frown lines, supported by a Phase 3 trial.
card.note: Prescription-only injectable; limited independent literature so far.

quick.overview:
Relfydess is a liquid botulinum toxin A from Galderma that needs no reconstitution. It is aimed at frown lines.

Its Phase 3 READY-1 trial compared it with placebo in adults with moderate-to-severe glabellar lines.
quick.mechanism: Like other type A toxins, it weakens injected muscles by blocking nerve signals to them.
quick.risks: It is a prescription injectable. Trial safety findings were not reviewed here, and off-label uses appear only as case reports.
